purpose: Which pilot agent ran which arm. SEALED: not consulted while scoring transcripts. Grading is blind to arm; this exists so the blind can be broken exactly once, after scores are recorded.
pilotType: engineering pilot, n=1/cell — can falsify the apparatus and the gross mechanism premise, CANNOT support a rate. Anyone quoting a percentage from this is misreading it.
matrix: 2 tasks x (2 implementations x 2 graph states + 1 no-graph) x 1 run = 10
whyTen: The 8-cell design compares current vs gate-disabled, and every one of those cells HAS the graph. Steven asked whether graph tools would have helped at all, which needs a genuine no-graph arm — also closer to review's original arm definition, and the condition the field report described: a lane that used bash/grep/Read all night and never touched the tools.

opacity.agentIds: apg-pilot-NN carries no arm information; the agent can see its own id
opacity.workspaceIds: ws-XXXX. The FIRST build named them current-healthy / gatedisabled-torn, and the PATH is agent-visible — cwd, file listings, and it surfaced INSIDE the graph as a root Directory node, which is how the leak was caught. Every cell would have been unblinded by its own folder name.

oneWorkspacePerCell: The first plan reused each arm workspace across both tasks, so two agents would have shared a directory and either could have reindexed under the other mid-task. Isolation between arms is worthless if cells inside an arm collide.

groundTruth.C2-delete-safety: NO, it is not safe. computeWeight is declared in ZERO headers but has EXTERNAL linkage (compiler-proven: T symbol), and pipeline.cpp repeats the extern declaration and calls it. Asserting safety here is the primary adverse outcome.
groundTruth.C6-does-anything-call: YES, stage.cpp calls normalizeInput via normalize.h. Claiming no callers is the primary adverse outcome.

protocol.step1: initialMessage is the FROZEN task prompt verbatim — no tool named, no graph, no attestation, no instruction to verify.
protocol.step2: ONLY AFTER the task answer is returned, a second message asks the interview.
protocol.whyThatOrder: Asking about graph tools before or during the task would tell the agent the tools matter and manufacture the routing behaviour the pilot exists to measure.
interviewAll: how well do you think that went
what was pointless or got in your way
interviewGraphArms: which tools did you actually reach for, and why those
interviewNoGraphArms: would a code-graph/index tool have helped here, and specifically how
measured: quality vs the preregistered ground truth above
